intention: Replace charging's hardcoded 62.0 kWh pack capacity with a real, measured value. A monthly job inside charging pools each vehicle's valid charge records (USER manual entries and DONE supercharger sessions only, RD2), drops rows below a 15-point battery delta, and stores the median in charging.monthly_effective_capacity keyed on (tesla_id, effective_period). packCapacityKWh reads that table and still returns 62.0 until a month is measured. Self-contained: charging owns every input row, so no cross-module port and no import cycle exist.

decisions.decision: Added candidate_count to the approved DDL. sample_count keeps its post-gate meaning (design D1). A stored row always has candidate_count >= 1.
decisions.why: sample_count alone cannot tell 'no measurable charges' from '20 charges, all too small'. The migration was unwritten, so the column cost nothing; later it would need a migration.

decisions.decision: The leader finished the candidate_count edit itself after the charging worker died on a session rate limit mid-task. Worker had completed the DDL, the COMMENT ON, and the upsert; the leader wrote D1, Risk 1, the decision mapping, fixtures C4/C5/C6/C12/C13 and the tasks.md gate note.
decisions.why: A fresh worker would re-read the whole doc pack for a doc edit the leader already had full context for. Leaving artifacts half-edited was the worse option.

decisions.decision: Accepted the worker's own design calls unchanged: D1's post-gate sample_count reasoning, D2 (no row when a tesla_id has zero valid rows), D3 (the packCapacityLookup narrow interface), the no-new-index decision with a recorded revisit trigger, and teslaID filtering in Go rather than a second SQL path.
decisions.why: Each was argued from the code and none contradicted a roadmap decision. The worker also escalated the one genuinely open question instead of guessing, which is what caught the candidate_count gap.

decisions.decision: Added design.md D9 as a standing rule: the monthly capacity estimator stays split into a gate (estimateEffectiveCapacity) and a method (median). A future estimation method is a new sibling function with median's exact signature, func(gated []capacitySample) float64 -- never an edit to median, never inlined into the gate. The seam widened from []float64 to []capacitySample and the sort moved inside median. No strategy type and no method column: the rule is a doc rule plus a signature. D9 also prices the future second-column path so a later agent does not re-derive it. New test A9 pins the seam.
decisions.why: The owner expects to try another calculation over the same input data later -- for testing, or stored in a new column alongside the median. A []float64 seam drops BatteryDeltaPct, so a delta-weighted or trimmed method would have to reshape estimateEffectiveCapacity's body, the exact code tests A1-A5 pin. No code exists yet (status: proposed), so the fix cost nothing.
